Evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena anandheneva andhena viya bhavitabbaṃ, araññepi gocaragāme piṇḍāya carantenapi rajanīyesu rūpasaddagandharasaphoṭṭhabbadhammesu andhena badhirena mūgena viya bhavitabbaṃ, na nimittaṃ gahetabbaṃ, nānubyañjanaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, kukkuṭassa catutthaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therena mahākaccāyanena –

“Furthermore, great king, a rooster, though possessing eyes, is blind at night. Just so, great king, a yogi, a practitioner, even though not blind, should behave as if blind—whether wandering for alms in the forest or in the alms-village. When encountering forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangible objects, and mental objects that are enticing, one should be like a blind man, a deaf man, or a mute—not grasping at the sign, not grasping at the particulars. This, great king, is the fourth characteristic of a rooster to be adopted. This was also spoken, great king, by the elder Mahākaccāyana:

‘Cakkhumāssa yathā andho, sotavā badhiro yathā;

Paññavāssa jivhāvassa (sī. pī.) yathā mūgo, balavā dubbaloriva;

Attaatthe atha atthe (sī. pī.) samuppanne, sayetha matasāyika’nti.

“‘Though having eyes, be as if blind; though having ears, be as if deaf; though wise, be as if mute; though strong, be as if weak. When personal gain arises, one should lie down as if dead.’”

“Puna [M 0.0350] caparaṃ, mahārāja, kukkuṭo leḍḍudaṇḍalaguḷamuggarehi paripātiyantopi sakaṃ gehaṃ na vijahati. Evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena cīvarakammaṃ karontenapi navakammaṃ karontenapi vattappaṭivattaṃ karontenapi uddisantenapi uddisāpentenapi yoniso manasikāro na vijahitabbo, sakaṃ kho panetaṃ, mahārāja, yogino gehaṃ, yadidaṃ yoniso manasikāro[V 0.0334]. Idaṃ, mahārāja, kukkuṭassa pañcamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ[P 0.0368]. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena ‘ko ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno gocaro sako pettiko visayo? Yadidaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’ti. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therena sāriputtena dhammasenāpatināpi –

“Furthermore, great king, a rooster, even when being pelted with clods, sticks, clubs, or mallets, does not abandon its own home. In the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner—even while doing robe-work, doing new construction, performing routine duties, reciting, or having others recite—should not abandon appropriate attention. For this, great king, is the yogi's own home, namely, appropriate attention. This, great king, is the fifth characteristic of a rooster to be adopted. This was also spoken, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods: ‘And what, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu’s own range, his ancestral territory? It is the four foundations of mindfulness.’ This was also spoken, great king, by the elder Sāriputta, the general of the Dhamma:

“‘Yathā sudanto mātaṅgo, sakaṃ soṇḍaṃ na maddati;

Bhakkhābhakkhaṃ vijānāti, attano vuttikappanaṃ.

“‘Just as a well-tamed elephant does not trample on its own trunk, and knows what is edible and inedible for its own sustenance,

“‘Tatheva buddhaputtena, appamattena vā pana;

Jinavacanaṃ na madditabbaṃ, manasikāravaruttama’”nti.

“‘so too, a son of the Buddha, being heedful, should not transgress the Victor's teaching, that supreme and best attention.’”

Kukkuṭaṅgapañho dutiyo.

The Second Question on the Qualities of a Rooster.

3. Kalandakaṅgapañho

3. The Question on the Qualities of a Squirrel

3. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘kalandakassa ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba’nti yaṃ vadesi, katamaṃ taṃ ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba”nti? “Yathā, mahārāja, kalandako paṭisattumhi opatante naṅguṭṭhaṃ papphoṭetvā mahantaṃ katvā teneva naṅguṭṭhalaguḷena paṭisattuṃ paṭibāhati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena kilesasattumhi opatante satipaṭṭhānalaguḷaṃ papphoṭetvā mahantaṃ katvā teneva satipaṭṭhānalaguḷena sabbakilesā paṭibāhitabbā. Idaṃ, mahārāja, kalandakassa ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therena cūḷapanthakena –

3. “Venerable Nāgasena, you said that ‘one characteristic of the squirrel should be adopted.’ What is that one characteristic that should be adopted?” “Just as, great king, when an enemy approaches, the squirrel flicks its tail, making it large, and with that very tail-club it wards off the enemy, in the same way, great king, when the enemy of defilements approaches, the yogi, a practitioner, should flick the club of the foundations of mindfulness, making it large, and with that very club of the foundations of mindfulness, all defilements should be warded off. This, great king, is the one characteristic of the squirrel that should be adopted. This was also spoken, great king, by the elder Cūḷapanthaka:

‘Yadā kilesā opatanti, sāmaññaguṇadhaṃsanā;

Satipaṭṭhānalaguḷena, hantabbā te punappuna’”nti.

“‘When defilements approach, destroying the qualities of recluseship, with the club of the foundations of mindfulness, they should be struck down again and again.’”

Kalandakaṅgapañho tatiyo.

The Third Question on the Qualities of a Squirrel.

4. Dīpiniyaṅgapañho

4. The Question on the Characteristic of the Female Leopard

4. “Bhante [V 0.0335][M 0.0351] nāgasena, ‘dīpiniyā ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba’nti yaṃ vadesi, katamaṃ taṃ ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba”nti? “Yathā, mahārāja, dīpinī sakiṃ yeva gabbhaṃ gaṇhāti, na punappunaṃ purisaṃ upeti? Evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena āyatiṃ paṭisandhiṃ uppattiṃ gabbhaseyyaṃ cutiṃ bhedaṃ khayaṃ vināsaṃ saṃsārabhayaṃ duggatiṃ visamaṃ sampīḷitaṃ disvā ‘punabbhave [P 0.0369] nappaṭisandahissāmī’ti yoniso manasikāro karaṇīyo. Idaṃ, mahārāja, dīpiniyā ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena suttanipāte dhaniyagopālakasutte –

4. “Venerable Nāgasena, you said that ‘one characteristic of the female leopard should be adopted.’ What is that one characteristic to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, a female leopard conceives only once and does not approach a male again, so too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, having seen future rebirth, arising, lying in the womb, passing away, breaking up, decay, destruction, the peril of saṃsāra, the bad destinations, the uneven and oppressed states, should wisely resolve, ‘I will not be relinked again in a future existence.’ This, great king, is the one characteristic of the female leopard that should be adopted. This was also spoken, great king, by the Blessed One, the god above gods, in the Sutta Nipāta, in the Dhaniyagopālaka Sutta:—

“‘Usabhoriva chetva bandhanāni, nāgo pūtilataṃva dālayitvā;

Nāhaṃ punupessaṃ gabbhaseyyaṃ, atha ce patthayasī pavassa devā’”ti.

“‘Like a bull, having broken its bonds, like an elephant, having torn apart a rotten creeper, I will not enter a womb again. So if you wish, O god, let it rain!’”

Dīpiniyaṅgapañho catuttho.

The fourth question, on the characteristic of the female leopard.

5. Dīpikaṅgapañho

5. The Question on the Characteristics of the Leopard

5. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘dīpikassa dve aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni dve aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, dīpiko araññe tiṇagahanaṃ vā vanagahanaṃ vā pabbatagahanaṃ vā nissāya nilīyitvā mige gaṇhāti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena vivekaṃ sevitabbaṃ araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ appasaddaṃ appanigghosaṃ vijanavātaṃ manussarāhaseyyakaṃ paṭisallānasāruppaṃ; vivekaṃ sevamāno hi, mahārāja, yogī yogāvacaro nacirasseva chaḷabhiññāsu ca vasibhāvaṃ pāpuṇāti. Idaṃ, mahārāja, dīpikassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therehi dhammasaṅgāhakehi –

5. “Venerable Nāgasena, you say that ‘two characteristics of a leopard should be adopted.’ What are these two characteristics that should be adopted?” “Just as, great king, a leopard, relying on a thicket of grass, a thicket of woods, or a mountain thicket, lies in wait and catches beasts; so too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should resort to a secluded lodging: a forest, the root of a tree, a mountain, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a jungle thicket, an open space, a heap of straw—a place with little sound and noise, secluded from people, suitable for withdrawal. For by resorting to seclusion, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, will before long attain mastery over the six higher knowledges. This, great king, is the first characteristic of a leopard that should be adopted. This has been said, great king, by the elders, the compilers of the Dhamma:

“‘Yathāpi [V 0.0336][M 0.0352] dīpiko nāma, nilīyitvā gaṇhate gaṇhatī (sī. pī.) mige;

Tathevāyaṃ buddhaputto, yuttayogo vipassako;

Araññaṃ pavisitvāna, gaṇhāti phalamuttama’nti.

“‘Just as a leopard, lying in wait, catches beasts; so too this son of the Buddha, devoted to the practice, an insight meditator, having entered the forest, obtains the supreme fruit.’”

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, dīpiko yaṃ kiñci pasuṃ vadhitvā vāmena passena patitaṃ na bhakkheti. Evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena veḷudānena vā pattadānena vā pupphadānena vā phaladānena vā sinānadānena vā mattikādānena vā cuṇṇadānena vā dantakaṭṭhadānena [P 0.0370] vā mukhodakadānena vā cātukamyatāya vā muggasupyatāya muggasuppatāya (sī. pī.) vā pāribhaṭa pāribhaṭṭatāya (sī. pī.) yatāya vā jaṅghapesanīyena vā vejjakammena vā dūtakammena vā pahiṇagamanena vā piṇḍapaṭipiṇḍena vā dānānuppadānena vā vatthuvijjāya vā nakkhattavijjāya vā aṅgavijjāya nagavijjāya (ka.) vā aññataraññatarena vā buddhappaṭikuṭṭhena micchājīvena nipphāditaṃ bhojanaṃ na bhuñjitabbaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ (sī. pī.) vāmena passena patitaṃ pasuṃ viya dīpiko. Idaṃ, mahārāja, dīpikassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therena sāriputtena dhammasenāpatinā –

“Furthermore, great king, a leopard does not eat any beast it has killed that has fallen on its left side. So too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should not eat food that has been produced by any kind of wrong livelihood condemned by the Buddha, such as: giving bamboo, giving leaves, giving flowers, giving fruit, giving bathing soap, giving clay, giving powder, giving tooth-sticks, giving water for rinsing the mouth; or by flattery, hinting, acting as a nursemaid, running errands, practicing medicine, acting as a messenger, sending others on errands, exchanging one alms-gift for another, giving a gift in return for another; or by the science of sites, astrology, or the science of bodily marks—like the leopard and the beast that has fallen on its left side. This, great king, is the second characteristic of the leopard that should be adopted. This was spoken, great king, by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:”

“‘Vacīviññattivipphārā, uppannaṃ madhupāyasaṃ;

Sace bhutto bhaveyyāhaṃ, sājīvo garahito mama.

“‘Through the diffusion of verbal hints, honeyed milk-rice was produced; if I were to eat it, my livelihood would be blameworthy.’

“‘Yadipi me antaguṇaṃ, nikkhamitvā bahī care;

Neva bhindeyyamājīvaṃ, cajamānopi jīvita’”nti.

“‘Even if my entrails, having come out, were to wander outside, I would not break my livelihood, even while giving up my life.’”

Dīpikaṅgapañho pañcamo.

The fifth question, on the characteristics of the leopard.

6. Kummaṅgapañho

6. The Question on the Characteristics of the Tortoise

6. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘kummassa pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, kummo udakacaro udakeyeva vāsaṃ kappeti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena sabbapāṇabhūtapuggalānaṃ hitānukampinā mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ pharitvā viharitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, kummassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

6. “Venerable Nāgasena, you say that ‘five characteristics of a tortoise should be adopted.’ What are those five characteristics that should be adopted?” “Just as, great king, a tortoise is an aquatic creature and makes its home in the water, so too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should dwell pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will—compassionate for the welfare of all living beings and creatures. This, great king, is the first characteristic of a tortoise that should be adopted.”

“Puna [V 0.0337][M 0.0353] caparaṃ, mahārāja, kummo udake uppilavanto sīsaṃ ukkhipitvā yadi koci passati, tattheva nimujjati gāḷhamogāhati ‘mā maṃ te puna passeyyu’nti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena kilesesu opatantesu ārammaṇasare nimujjitabbaṃ gāḷhamogāhitabbaṃ ‘mā maṃ kilesā puna passeyyu’nti. Idaṃ, mahārāja, kummassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, great king, just as a tortoise, while floating in the water, raises its head, and if it sees someone, it immediately dives down and submerges itself deeply, thinking, ‘May they not see me again!’; so too, great king, when the defilements descend, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should dive down and submerge himself deeply in the lake of his meditation subject, thinking, ‘May the defilements not see me again!’ This, great king, is the second characteristic of the tortoise that should be adopted.”

“Puna caparaṃ[P 0.0371], mahārāja, kummo udakato nikkhamitvā kāyaṃ otāpeti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena nisajjaṭṭhānasayanacaṅkamato mānasaṃ nīharitvā sammappadhāne mānasaṃ otāpetabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, kummassa tatiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, great king, just as a tortoise, having come out of the water, basks its body in the sun; so too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should withdraw his mind from the postures of sitting, standing, lying down, and walking, and ‘bask’ his mind in the right exertions. This, great king, is the third characteristic of a tortoise that should be adopted.”

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, kummo pathaviṃ khaṇitvā vivitte vāsaṃ kappeti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena lābhasakkārasilokaṃ pajahitvā suññaṃ vivittaṃ kānanaṃ vanapatthaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ appasaddaṃ appanigghosaṃ pavivittamogāhitvā vivitte yeva vāsaṃ upagantabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, kummassa catutthaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therena upasenena vaṅgantaputtena –

“Furthermore, great king, a tortoise digs into the earth and makes its dwelling in a secluded place. So too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should abandon gain, honor, and fame, and having entered a secluded place—an empty place, a forest, a wilderness, a mountain, a ravine, a mountain cave, a place with little sound and noise, utterly secluded—he should take up his dwelling in seclusion. This, great king, is the fourth characteristic of the tortoise that should be adopted. This was spoken, great king, by the Elder Upasena Vaṅgantaputta:”

“‘Vivittaṃ appanigghosaṃ, vāḷamiganisevitaṃ;

Seve senāsanaṃ bhikkhu, paṭisallānakāraṇā’ti.

“‘A bhikkhu should resort to a lodging that is secluded, with little noise, frequented by beasts of prey, for the sake of withdrawal.’”

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, kummo cārikaṃ caramāno yadi kañci passati vā, saddaṃ suṇāti vā, soṇḍipañcamāni aṅgāni sake kapāle nidahitvā appossukko tuṇhībhūto tiṭṭhati kāyamanurakkhanto, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena sabbattha rūpasaddagandharasaphoṭṭhabbadhammesu āpatantesu chasu dvāresu saṃvarakavāṭaṃ anugghāṭetvā mānasaṃ samodahitvā saṃvaraṃ katvā satena sampajānena vihātabbaṃ samaṇadhammaṃ anurakkhamānena. Idaṃ, mahārāja, kummassa pañcamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena saṃyuttanikāyavare kummūpamasuttante –

“Furthermore, great king, when a tortoise is wandering about, if it sees or hears anything, it withdraws its five limbs, including its neck, into its own shell and remains unconcerned and silent, protecting its body. So too, great king, when sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, or mental phenomena impinge upon the six sense doors, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should not open the gate of restraint, but should compose his mind, establish restraint, and dwell with mindfulness and clear comprehension, guarding the practice of a recluse. This, great king, is the fifth characteristic of the tortoise that should be adopted. This was spoken, great king, by the Blessed One, the god of gods, in the excellent Saṃyutta Nikāya, in the Kummopama Sutta:”

“‘Kummova [M 0.0354] aṅgāni sake kapāle, samodahaṃ bhikkhu manovitakke;

Anissito [P 0.0372] aññamaheṭhayāno, parinibbutonūpavadeyya kañcī’”ti.

“‘Just as a tortoise draws its limbs into its own shell, so a bhikkhu should compose his thoughts. Independent, not harming another, fully quenched, he would not disparage anyone.’”

Kummaṅgapañho chaṭṭho.

The sixth question, on the characteristics of the tortoise.

7. Vaṃsaṅgapañho

7. The Question on the Characteristic of the Bamboo

7. “Bhante [V 0.0338] nāgasena, ‘vaṃsassa ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba’nti yaṃ vadesi, katamaṃ taṃ ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba”nti? “Yathā, mahārāja, vaṃso yattha vāto, tattha anulometi, nāññatthamanudhāvati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena yaṃ buddhena bhagavatā bhāsitaṃ navaṅgaṃ satthu sāsanaṃ, taṃ anulomayitvā kappiye anavajje ṭhatvā samaṇadhammaṃ yeva pariyesitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, vaṃsassa ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ mahārāja therena rāhulena –

7. “Venerable Nāgasena, you say that ‘one quality of a bamboo should be adopted.’ What is that one quality that should be adopted?” “Just as, great king, a bamboo bends in the direction of the wind and does not run in another direction, so too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should conform to the nine-limbed teaching of the Master spoken by the Blessed One, the Buddha, and, having established himself in what is allowable and blameless, should seek only the qualities of a recluse. This, great king, is the one quality of a bamboo that should be adopted. This has also been said, great king, by the Elder Rāhula:

“‘Navaṅgaṃ buddhavacanaṃ, anulometvāna sabbadā;

Kappiye anavajjasmiṃ, ṭhatvāpāyaṃ samuttari’”nti.

“‘Always conforming to the nine-limbed word of the Buddha, and standing in what is suitable and blameless, one crosses beyond the plane of misery.’”

Vaṃsaṅgapañho sattamo.

The seventh question, on the characteristic of the bamboo.

8. Cāpaṅgapañho

8. The Question on the Characteristic of the Bow

8. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘cāpassa ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba’nti yaṃ vadesi, katamaṃ taṃ ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba”nti? “Yathā, mahārāja, cāpo sutacchito namito mito (sī. pī. ka.) yāvaggamūlaṃ samakameva anunamati nappaṭitthambhati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena theranavamajjhimasamakesu anunamitabbaṃ nappaṭipharitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, cāpassa ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena vidhura [puṇṇaka] jātake –

8. "Venerable Nāgasena, you said that 'one quality of a bow should be adopted.' What is that one quality that should be adopted?" "Just as, great king, a well-smoothed bow, when bent, bends evenly from tip to base and does not stiffen, so too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, should be evenly compliant towards elders, newly ordained bhikkhus, and those of middle standing, and should not be resistant. This, great king, is the one quality of a bow that should be adopted. This has been said, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods, in the Vidhura Jātaka:

“‘Cāpovūnudaro [M 0.0355] dhīro, vaṃso vāpi pakampaye cāpo vā nuna me dhīro, vaṃsova anulomayaṃ (sī. pī. ka.);

Paṭilomaṃ na vatteyya, sa rājavasatiṃ vase’”ti.

"'The wise one should be slender-waisted like a bow and pliant like a bamboo. He should not act contrarily; such a one may dwell in the king's service.'"

Cāpaṅgapañho aṭṭhamo.

The Question on the Quality of the Bow, the Eighth.

9. Vāyasaṅgapañho

9. The Question on the Qualities of the Crow

9. “Bhante [V 0.0339] nāgasena, ‘vāyasassa dve aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni dve aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, vāyaso āsaṅkitaparisaṅkito yattappayatto [P 0.0373] carati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena āsaṅkitaparisaṅkitena yattapayattena upaṭṭhitāya satiyā saṃvutehi indriyehi caritabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, vāyasassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

9. "Venerable Nāgasena, you said that 'two qualities of a crow should be adopted.' What are those two qualities that should be adopted?" "Just as, great king, a crow moves about suspiciously and with circumspection, restrained and diligent, so too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, should move about suspiciously and with circumspection, restrained and diligent, with mindfulness established and with senses guarded. This, great king, is the first quality of a crow that should be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, vāyaso yaṃ kiñci bhojanaṃ disvā ñātīhi saṃvibhajitvā bhuñjati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena ye te lābhā dhammikā dhammaladdhā antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampi, tathārūpehi lābhehi paṭivibhattabhoginā bhavitabbaṃ sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi. Idaṃ, mahārāja, vāyasassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therena sāriputtena dhammasenāpatinā –

"Furthermore, great king, when a crow sees any food, it eats only after sharing it with its kinsmen. So too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, should be one who partakes of things only after sharing any gains that are righteous and righteously obtained—even if it is only the contents of his alms-bowl—with his virtuous companions in the holy life. This, great king, is the second quality of a crow that should be adopted. This has been said, great king, by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:

“‘Sace me upanāmenti, yathāladdhaṃ tapassino;

Sabbe saṃvibhajitvāna, tato bhuñjāmi bhojana’”nti.

"'If ascetics bring to me what they have obtained, I eat my meal only after having shared it with all.'"

Vāyasaṅgapañho navamo.

The Question on the Qualities of the Crow, the Ninth.

10. Makkaṭaṅgapañho

10. The Question on the Qualities of the Monkey

10. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘makkaṭassa dve aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni dve aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, makkaṭo vāsamupagacchanto tathārūpe okāse mahatimahārukkhe pavivitte sabbaṭṭhakasākhe sabbatthakasākhe (syā.), sabbaṭṭhasākhe (ka.) bhīruttāṇe vāsamupagacchati, evameva kho, mahārāja[M 0.0356], yoginā yogāvacarena lajjiṃ pesalaṃ sīlavantaṃ kalyāṇadhammaṃ bahussutaṃ dhammadharaṃ vinayadharaṃ piyaṃ garubhāvanīyaṃ vattāraṃ vacanakkhamaṃ ovādakaṃ viññāpakaṃ sandassakaṃ samādapakaṃ samuttejakaṃ sampahaṃsakaṃ evarūpaṃ kalyāṇamittaṃ ācariyaṃ nissāya viharitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, makkaṭassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

10. "Venerable Nāgasena, you said that 'two qualities of a monkey should be adopted.' What are those two qualities that should be adopted?" "Just as, great king, a monkey seeking a dwelling resorts to a great and mighty tree in a secluded place, one with dense foliage providing a refuge for the fearful, so too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, should dwell in dependence on a good friend and teacher who is conscientious, amiable, virtuous, of good qualities, learned, a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, dear, worthy of respect, an articulate speaker, patient with words, an advisor, an instructor, one who explains, incites, inspires, and gladdens. This, great king, is the first quality of a monkey that should be adopted.

“Puna [V 0.0340] caparaṃ, mahārāja, makkaṭo rukkhe yeva carati tiṭṭhati nisīdati, yadi niddaṃ okkamati, tattheva rattiṃ vāsamanubhavati. Evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena pavanābhimukhena bhavitabbaṃ, pavane yeva ṭhānacaṅkamanisajjāsayanaṃ [P 0.0374] niddaṃ okkamitabbaṃ, tattheva satipaṭṭhānamanubhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, makkaṭassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therena sāriputtena dhammasenāpatinā –

"Furthermore, great king, a monkey moves about, stands, and sits only in a tree; if it settles down to sleep, it spends the night right there. So too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, should be one who is intent on the forest. He should stand, walk, sit, lie down, and settle down to sleep only in the forest; right there he should experience the establishments of mindfulness. This, great king, is the second quality of a monkey that should be adopted. This has been said, great king, by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:

“‘Caṅkamantopi tiṭṭhanto, nisajjāsayanena vā;

Pavane sobhate bhikkhu, pavanantaṃva vaṇṇita’”nti.

"'Whether walking or standing, or by sitting or lying down, a bhikkhu is beautiful in the forest, like a praised forest-fringe.'"

Makkaṭaṅgapañho dasamo.

The Question on the Qualities of the Monkey, the Tenth.

Gadrabhavaggo paṭhamo.

The Chapter on the Donkey, the First.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Gadrabho ceva ghorassaro ca (sī. syā. pī.) kukkuṭo, kalando dīpini dīpiko;

Kummo vaṃso ca cāpo ca, vāyaso atha makkaṭoti.

The donkey and the cock, the squirrel, the pantheress, and the panther; the tortoise, bamboo, and bow, the crow and then the monkey.

2. Samuddavaggo

The Chapter on the Ocean

1. Lābulataṅgapañho

The Question on the Quality of the Gourd Creeper

1. “Bhante [V 0.0341][M 0.0357] nāgasena, ‘lābulatāya ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba’nti yaṃ vadesi, katamaṃ taṃ ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba”nti? “Yathā, mahārāja, lābulatā tiṇe vā kaṭṭhe vā latāya vā soṇḍikāhi ālambitvā tassūpari vaḍḍhati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena arahatte abhivaḍḍhitukāmena manasā ārammaṇaṃ ālambitvā arahatte abhivaḍḍhitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, lābulatāya ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therena sāriputtena dhammasenāpatinā –

2. “Venerable Nāgasena, you say, ‘One quality of the gourd creeper should be adopted.’ Which is that one quality to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, a gourd creeper grows upwards by clinging with its tendrils to grass, wood, or another creeper, so too, great king, a yogi devoted to the practice, desiring to grow into arahantship, should grow into arahantship by taking a mental object as support. This, great king, is the one quality of the gourd creeper to be adopted. And this was said, great king, by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:

“‘Yathā lābulatā nāma, tiṇe kaṭṭhe latāya vā;

Ālambitvā soṇḍikāhi, tato vaḍḍhati uppari.

1. “‘Just as a gourd creeper, clinging with its tendrils to grass, wood, or another creeper, grows upwards from there,

“‘Tatheva buddhaputtena, arahattaphalakāminā;

Ārammaṇaṃ ālambitvā, vaḍḍhitabbaṃ asekkhaphale’”ti.

1. “‘Even so a son of the Buddha, desiring the fruit of arahantship, taking an object as support, should grow into the fruit of one beyond training.’”

Lābulataṅgapañho paṭhamo.

The First Question on the Quality of the Gourd Creeper.

2. Padumaṅgapañho

The Question on the Qualities of the Lotus

2. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘padumassa tīṇi aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni tīṇi aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti[P 0.0375]? “Yathā, mahārāja, padumaṃ udake jātaṃ udake saṃvaddhaṃ anupalittaṃ udakena, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena kule gaṇe lābhe yase [V 0.0342] sakkāre sammānanāya paribhogapaccayesu ca sabbattha anupalittena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, padumassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

“Venerable Nāgasena, you say, ‘Three qualities of the lotus should be adopted.’ What are those three qualities to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, a lotus is born in the water and grows up in the water but is unsullied by the water, so too, great king, a yogi devoted to the practice should remain unsullied in every way by family, group, gain, fame, honor, respect, and the requisites for use. This, great king, is the first quality of the lotus to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, padumaṃ udakā accuggamma ṭhāti. Evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena sabbalokaṃ abhibhavitvā accuggamma lokuttaradhamme ṭhātabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, padumassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

2. “Furthermore, great king, the lotus rises up out of the water and stands there. Even so, great king, a yogi devoted to the practice, having overcome and risen above the entire world, should stand firm in the supramundane states. This, great king, is the second quality of the lotus to be adopted.

“Puna [M 0.0358] caparaṃ, mahārāja, padumaṃ appamattakenapi anilena eritaṃ calati. Evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena appamattakesupi kilesesu saṃyamo karaṇīyo, bhayadassāvinā viharitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, padumassa tatiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena ‘aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesū’ti.

2. “Furthermore, great king, a lotus trembles when stirred by even a slight breeze. Even so, great king, a yogi devoted to the practice should exercise restraint in regard to the slightest defilements and should dwell seeing the danger in them. This, great king, is the third quality of the lotus to be adopted. And this was said, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods: ‘Seeing danger in the slightest faults, one undertakes and trains in the training rules.’”

Padumaṅgapañho dutiyo.

The Second Question on the Qualities of the Lotus.

3. Bījaṅgapañho

The Question on the Qualities of a Seed

3. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘bījassa dve aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni dve aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, bījaṃ appakampi samānaṃ bhaddake khette vuttaṃ deve sammā dhāraṃ pavecchante subahūni phalāni anudassati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena yathā paṭipāditaṃ sīlaṃ kevalaṃ sāmaññaphalamanudassati. Evaṃ sammā paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, bījassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

“Venerable Nāgasena, you say, ‘Two qualities of a seed should be adopted.’ What are those two qualities to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, a seed, though small, when sown in a good field while the sky-god sends down rain properly, yields abundant fruit, so too, great king, for a yogi devoted to the practice, the virtue that is rightly undertaken yields the entire fruit of recluseship. Thus one should practice rightly. This, great king, is the first quality of a seed to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, bījaṃ suparisodhite khette ropitaṃ khippameva saṃvirūhati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena mānasaṃ supariggahitaṃ suññāgāre parisodhitaṃ satipaṭṭhānakhettavare khittaṃ khippameva virūhati. Idaṃ, mahārāja, bījassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ[P 0.0376]. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therena anuruddhena –

“Furthermore, great king, just as a seed planted in a well-cleared field quickly sprouts, so too, great king, the mind of a yogi devoted to the practice—well-grasped and purified in an empty dwelling—when sown in the excellent field of the foundations of mindfulness, quickly grows. This, great king, is the second quality of the seed to be adopted. And this was said, great king, by the Elder Anuruddha:

“‘Yathāpi [V 0.0343] khette yathā khette (sī.) parisuddhe, bījañcassa patiṭṭhitaṃ;

Vipulaṃ tassa phalaṃ hoti, api toseti kassakaṃ.

“‘Just as in a purified field, when a seed is well-established, its fruit is abundant and also pleases the farmer.

“‘Tatheva yogino cittaṃ, suññāgāre visodhitaṃ;

Satipaṭṭhānakhettamhi, khippameva virūhatī’”ti.

“‘Even so the yogi’s mind, purified in an empty dwelling, quickly grows in the field of the foundations of mindfulness.’”

Bījaṅgapañho tatiyo.

The Third Question on the Qualities of a Seed.

4. Sālakalyāṇikaṅgapañho

4. The Question on the Quality of the Sālakalyāṇikā Plant

4. “Bhante [M 0.0359] nāgasena, ‘sālakalyāṇikāya ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba’nti yaṃ vadesi, katamaṃ taṃ ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba”nti? “Yathā, mahārāja, sālakalyāṇikā nāma antopathaviyaṃ yeva abhivaḍḍhati hatthasatampi bhiyyopi, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena cattāri sāmaññaphalāni catasso paṭisambhidā chaḷabhiññāyo kevalañca samaṇadhammaṃ suññāgāre yeva paripūrayitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, sālakalyāṇikāya ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therena rāhulena –

4. “Venerable Nāgasena, you say, ‘One quality of the Sālakalyāṇikā plant should be adopted.’ What is that one quality to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, the Sālakalyāṇikā plant grows right within the earth, even to a hundred cubits or more, so too, great king, a yogi devoted to the practice should bring to fulfillment the four fruits of recluseship, the four analytical knowledges, the six direct knowledges, and the entire recluse’s state, only in an empty dwelling. This, great king, is the one quality of the Sālakalyāṇikā plant to be adopted. And this was said, great king, by the Elder Rāhula:

“‘Sālakalyāṇikā nāma, pādapo dharaṇīruho;

Antopathaviyaṃ yeva, satahatthopi vaḍḍhati.

“‘The Sālakalyāṇikā is a tree, growing from the earth; right within the earth it grows, even a hundred cubits.

“‘Yathā kālamhi sampatte, paripākena so dumo;

Uggañchitvāna ekāhaṃ, satahatthopi vaḍḍhati.

“‘When its time has come, that tree, being mature, shoots up in a single day and grows even a hundred cubits.

“‘Evamevāhaṃ mahāvīra, sālakalyāṇikā viya;

Abbhantare suññāgāre, dhammato abhivaḍḍhayi’”nti.

“‘Even so, O great hero, like the Sālakalyāṇikā, I grew by means of the Dhamma within an empty dwelling.’”

Sālakalyāṇikaṅgapañho catuttho.

The Fourth Question on the Quality of the Sālakalyāṇikā Plant.

5. Nāvaṅgapañho

5. The Question on the Qualities of a Boat

5. “Bhante [V 0.0344] nāgasena, ‘nāvāya tīṇi aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni tīṇi aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, nāvā bahuvidhadārusaṅghāṭasamavāyena bahumpi janaṃ tārayati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena ācārasīlaguṇavattappaṭivattabahuvidhadhammasaṅghāṭasamavāyena sadevako loko tārayitabbo. Idaṃ, mahārāja, nāvāya paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

5. “Venerable Nāgasena, you said, ‘Three qualities of a boat are to be adopted.’ What are those three qualities to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, a boat, by being constructed from a combination of various kinds of timber, carries many people across, so too, great king, a yogi, one devoted to the practice, should carry the world with its gods across by means of the combination of the manifold good qualities of conduct, virtue, and the performance of duties. This, great king, is the first quality of a boat to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, nāvā bahuvidhaūmitthanitavegavisaṭamāvaṭṭavegaṃ [P 0.0377] sahati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena bahuvidhakilesaūmivegaṃ lābhasakkārayasasilokapūjanavandanā parakulesu nindāpasaṃsāsukhadukkhasammānanavimānanabahuvidhadosaūmivegañca sahitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, nāvāya dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, great king, just as a boat withstands the force of the manifold waves, the roaring of the surf, and the swirling of whirlpools, so too, great king, a yogi, one devoted to the practice, should endure the force of the waves of the manifold defilements: gain, honor, fame, and renown; veneration and homage; blame and praise in other families; pleasure and pain; respect and disrespect; and the force of the waves of various corruptions. This, great king, is the second quality of a boat to be adopted.

“Puna [M 0.0360] caparaṃ, mahārāja, nāvā aparimitamanantamapāramakkhobhitagambhīre mahatimahāghose timitimiṅgalamakaramacchagaṇākule mahatimahāsamudde carati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena tiparivaṭṭa dvādasākāra catusaccābhisamayappaṭivedhe mānasaṃ sañcārayitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, nāvāya tatiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena saṃyuttanikāyavare saccasaṃyutte –

“Furthermore, great king, just as a boat travels on the great ocean—immeasurable, endless, shoreless, unagitated, deep, with a great roar, teeming with timis, timiṅgalas, makaras, and shoals of fish—so too, great king, a yogi, one devoted to the practice, should direct his mind to the realization and penetration of the Four Noble Truths with their three revolutions and twelve aspects. This, great king, is the third quality of a boat to be adopted. This was said, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods, in the excellent Saṃyutta Nikāya, in the Connected Discourses on the Truths:

“‘Vitakkentā ca kho tumhe, bhikkhave, “idaṃ dukkha”nti vitakkeyyātha, “ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo”ti vitakkeyyātha, “ayaṃ dukkhanirodho”ti vitakkeyyātha, “ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā”ti vitakkeyyāthā’”ti.

“‘Bhikkhus, when you are thinking, you should think: “This is suffering”; you should think: “This is the origin of suffering”; you should think: “This is the cessation of suffering”; you should think: “This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.”’”

Nāvaṅgapañho pañcamo.

The fifth question on the qualities of a boat.

6. Nāvālagganakaṅgapañho

6. The Question on the Qualities of an Anchor

6. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘nāvālagganakassa dve aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni [V 0.0345] tāni dve aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, nāvālagganakaṃ bahuūmijālākulavikkhobhitasalilatale mahatimahāsamudde nāvaṃ laggeti ṭhapeti, na deti disāvidisaṃ harituṃ, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena rāgadosamohūmijāle mahatimahāvitakkasampahāre cittaṃ laggetabbaṃ, na dātabbaṃ disāvidisaṃ harituṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, nāvālagganakassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

6. “Venerable Nāgasena, you said, ‘Two qualities of an anchor are to be adopted.’ What are those two qualities to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, an anchor, on the surface of the water of the great ocean, which is agitated and confused by a net of many waves, makes a boat fast and holds it steady, not allowing it to be carried away in any direction, so too, great king, a yogi, one devoted to the practice, should make his mind fast amidst the great assault of thoughts, not allowing it to be carried away in any direction by the net of waves of lust, hatred, and delusion. This, great king, is the first quality of an anchor to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, nāvālagganakaṃ na plavati na pilavati (sī. pī.) visīdati, hatthasatepi udake nāvaṃ laggeti ṭhānamupaneti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena lābhayasasakkāramānanavandanapūjanaapacitīsu lābhaggayasaggepi [P 0.0378] na plavitabbaṃ, sarīrayāpanamattake yeva cittaṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, nāvālagganakassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therena sāriputtena dhammasenāpatinā –

“Furthermore, great king, just as an anchor does not float but sinks down, and even in water a hundred cubits deep, it makes the boat fast and brings it to a standstill, so too, great king, a yogi, one devoted to the practice, should not float amidst gain, fame, honor, reverence, veneration, homage, and respect, even when at the peak of gain and fame. His mind should be established merely on what is sufficient for the maintenance of the body. This, great king, is the second quality of an anchor to be adopted. This was said, great king, by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:

“‘Yathā [M 0.0361] samudde lagganakaṃ, na plavati visīdati;

Tatheva lābhasakkāre, mā plavatha visīdathā’”ti.

“‘Just as an anchor in the ocean does not float but sinks down, so too, amidst gain and honor, do not float; sink down.’”

Nāvālagganakaṅgapañho chaṭṭho.

The sixth question on the qualities of an anchor.

7. Kūpaṅgapañho

7. The Question on the Quality of a Mast

7. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘kūpassa ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba’nti yaṃ vadesi, katamaṃ taṃ ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba”nti? “Yathā, mahārāja, kūpo rajjuñca varattañca laṅkārañca dhāreti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena satisampajaññasamannāgatena bhavitabbaṃ, abhikkante paṭikkante ālokite vilokite samiñjite pasārite saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe asite pīte khāyite sāyite uccārapassāvakamme gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārinā bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, kūpassa ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena ‘sato, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vihareyya sampajāno, ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī’”ti.

7. “Venerable Nāgasena, you said, ‘One quality of a mast is to be adopted.’ What is that one quality to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, a mast supports the ropes, the straps, and the rigging, so too, great king, a yogi, one devoted to the practice, should be endowed with mindfulness and clear comprehension. He should be one who acts with clear comprehension when going forward and returning; when looking ahead and looking aside; when bending and stretching his limbs; when wearing his robes and carrying his outer robe and bowl; when eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; when defecating and urinating; when walking, standing, sitting, falling asleep, waking up, talking, and keeping silent. This, great king, is the one quality of a mast to be adopted. This was said, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods: ‘A bhikkhu, bhikkhus, should dwell mindful and clearly comprehending. This is our instruction to you.’”

Kūpaṅgapañho sattamo.

The seventh question on the quality of a mast.

8. Niyāmakaṅgapañho

8. The Question on the Helmsman's Qualities

8. “Bhante [V 0.0346] nāgasena, ‘niyāmakassa tīṇi aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni tīṇi aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, niyāmako rattindivaṃ satataṃ samitaṃ appamatto yattappayatto nāvaṃ sāreti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena cittaṃ niyāmayamānena rattindivaṃ satataṃ samitaṃ appamattena yattappayattena yoniso manasikārena cittaṃ niyāmetabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, niyāmakassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena dhammapade –

8. “Venerable Nāgasena, you say, ‘Three qualities of a helmsman are to be adopted.’ What are those three qualities to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, a helmsman steers the ship day and night, constantly, continuously, heedfully, and striving, so too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, while steering his mind, should steer it day and night, constantly, continuously, heedfully, striving, and with wise attention. This, great king, is the first quality of a helmsman to be adopted. This was stated, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods, in the Dhammapada:

“‘Appamādaratā [P 0.0379] hotha, sacittamanurakkhatha;

Duggā uddharathattānaṃ, paṅke sannova sattova (sī. pī.) kuñjaro’ti.

“‘Delight in heedfulness, guard your own mind; lift yourselves from the mire, like an elephant sunk in the mud.’”

“Puna [M 0.0362] caparaṃ, mahārāja, niyāmakassa yaṃ kiñci mahāsamudde kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā, sabbaṃ taṃ viditaṃ hoti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena kusalākusalaṃ sāvajjānavajjaṃ hīnappaṇītaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgaṃ vijānitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, niyāmakassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, great king, whatever in the great ocean is good or bad is all known to the helmsman. So too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, should discern what is wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, and the counterparts of dark and bright states. This, great king, is the second quality of a helmsman to be adopted.”

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, niyāmako yante muddikaṃ deti ‘mā koci yantaṃ āmasitthā’ti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena citte saṃvaramuddikā dātabbā ‘mā kiñci pāpakaṃ akusalavitakkaṃ vitakkesī’ti, idaṃ, mahārāja, niyāmakassa tatiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena saṃyuttanikāyavare ‘mā, bhikkhave, pāpake akusale vitakke vitakkeyyātha, seyyathīdaṃ, kāmavitakkaṃ byāpādavitakkaṃ vihiṃsāvitakka’”nti.

“Furthermore, great king, a helmsman puts a seal on the rudder, thinking, ‘Let no one touch the rudder.’ So too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, should put a seal of restraint on his mind, thinking, ‘Let me not think any evil, unwholesome thoughts.’ This, great king, is the third quality of a helmsman to be adopted. This was stated, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods, in the excellent Saṃyutta Nikāya: ‘Bhikkhus, do not think evil, unwholesome thoughts, that is, thoughts of sensual pleasure, thoughts of ill will, and thoughts of cruelty.’”

Niyāmakaṅgapañho aṭṭhamo.

The Eighth Question on the Helmsman's Qualities.

9. Kammakāraṅgapañho

9. The Question on the Workman's Quality

9. “Bhante [V 0.0347] nāgasena, ‘kammakārassa ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba’nti yaṃ vadesi, katamaṃ taṃ ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabba”nti? “Yathā, mahārāja, kammakāro evaṃ cintayati ‘bhatako ahaṃ imāya nāvāya kammaṃ karomi, imāyāhaṃ nāvāya vāhasā bhattavetanaṃ labhāmi, na me pamādo karaṇīyo, appamādena me ayaṃ nāvā vāhetabbā’ti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena evaṃ cintayitabbaṃ ‘imaṃ kho ahaṃ cātumahābhūtikaṃ kāyaṃ sammasanto satataṃ samitaṃ appamatto upaṭṭhitassati sato sampajāno samāhito ekaggacitto jātijarābyādhimaraṇasokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccissāmīti appamādo me karaṇīyo’ti, idaṃ, mahārāja, kammakārassa ekaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therena sāriputtena dhammasenāpatinā –

9. “Venerable Nāgasena, you say, ‘One quality of a workman is to be adopted.’ What is that one quality to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, a workman thinks: ‘I am a hired hand working on this ship. By means of this ship’s passage I obtain my food and wages. I must not be heedless; with heedfulness I must work this ship.’ So too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, should think: ‘By contemplating this body composed of the four great elements—constantly, continuously, heedfully, with mindfulness established, mindful and clearly comprehending, concentrated, with a one-pointed mind—I will be freed from birth, aging, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I must be heedful.’ This, great king, is the one quality of a workman to be adopted. This was also stated, great king, by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:”

“‘Kāyaṃ [P 0.0380] imaṃ sammasatha, parijānātha punappunaṃ;

Kāye sabhāvaṃ disvāna, dukkhassantaṃ karissathā’ti.

“‘Contemplate this body, investigate it again and again; having seen the intrinsic nature of the body, you will make an end to suffering.’”

Kammakāraṅgapañho navamo.

The Ninth Question on the Workman's Quality.

10. Samuddaṅgapañho

10. The Question on the Ocean's Qualities

10. “Bhante [M 0.0363] nāgasena, ‘samuddassa pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, mahāsamuddo matena kuṇapena saddhiṃ na saṃvasati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena rāgadosamohamānadiṭṭhimakkhapaḷāsaissāmacchariyamāyāsāṭheyyakuṭilavisamaduccaritakilesamalehi saddhiṃ na saṃvasitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, samuddassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

10. “Venerable Nāgasena, you say, ‘Five qualities of the ocean are to be adopted.’ What are those five qualities to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, the great ocean does not associate with a dead corpse, so too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, should not associate with the stains of the defilements: lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong views, contempt, spite, envy, stinginess, deceit, fraud, crookedness, unevenness, and misconduct. This, great king, is the first quality of the ocean to be adopted.”

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, mahāsamuddo muttāmaṇiveḷuriyasaṅkhasilāpavāḷaphalikamaṇivividharatananicayaṃ dhārento pidahati, na bahi vikirati. Evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena maggaphalajhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattivipassanābhiññāvividhaguṇaratanāni adhigantvā [V 0.0348] pidahitabbāni, na bahi nīharitabbāni. Idaṃ, mahārāja, samuddassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, great king, the great ocean, holding a collection of various treasures—pearls, gems, beryl, conch, quartz, coral, and crystal—conceals them and does not scatter them about. So too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, having attained the various treasures of virtuous qualities—path, fruition, jhāna, liberation, concentration, attainment, insight, and direct knowledge—should keep them concealed and not display them outwardly. This, great king, is the second quality of the ocean to be adopted.”

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, mahāsamuddo mahantehi mahābhūtehi saddhiṃ saṃvasati. Evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena appicchaṃ santuṭṭhaṃ dhutavādaṃ sallekhavuttiṃ ācārasampannaṃ lajjiṃ pesalaṃ garuṃ bhāvanīyaṃ vattāraṃ vacanakkhamaṃ codakaṃ pāpagarahiṃ ovādakaṃ anusāsakaṃ viññāpakaṃ sandassakaṃ samādapakaṃ samuttejakaṃ sampahaṃsakaṃ kalyāṇamittaṃ sabrahmacāriṃ nissāya vasitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, mahāsamuddassa tatiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, great king, the great ocean associates with great beings. So too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, should live in dependence on a good friend, a fellow practitioner in the holy life, who is of few wishes, content, an exponent of ascetic practices, of austere living, accomplished in conduct, conscientious, amiable, grave, venerable, an admonisher, patient of speech, a reprover, a censor of evil, an advisor, an instructor, one who makes things clear, who shows the way, who encourages, who rouses, and who gladdens. This, great king, is the third quality of the great ocean to be adopted.”

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, mahāsamuddo navasalilasampuṇṇāhi gaṅgāyamunāaciravatīsarabhūmahīādīhi nadīsatasahassehi antalikkhe saliladhārāhi ca pūritopi sakaṃ velaṃ nātivattati. Evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena lābhasakkārasilokavandanamānanapūjanakāraṇā jīvitahetupi sañcicca sikkhāpadavītikkamo na karaṇīyo. Idaṃ, mahārāja, mahāsamuddassa [P 0.0381] catutthaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena –

“Furthermore, great king, the great ocean, though filled by hundreds of thousands of rivers—the Ganges, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, Mahī, and others—and by streams of water from the sky, does not transgress its own shore. So too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, should not intentionally transgress a training rule on account of gain, honor, fame, homage, respect, or veneration, not even for the sake of his life. This, great king, is the fourth quality of the great ocean to be adopted. This was stated, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods:”

‘Seyyathāpi, mahārāja pahārādha (sī. pī.), mahāsamuddo ṭhitadhammo velaṃ nātikkamati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yaṃ mahā sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ, taṃ mama sāvakā jīvitahetupi nātikkamantī’ti.

“‘Just as, great king, the great ocean is of a stable nature and does not transgress its shore, so too my disciples do not transgress the training rules I have laid down for them, not even for the sake of life.’”

“Puna [M 0.0364] caparaṃ, mahārāja, mahāsamuddo sabbasavantīhi gaṅgāyamunāaciravatīsarabhūmahīhi antalikkhe udakadhārāhipi na paripūrati. Evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena uddesaparipucchāsavanadhāraṇavinicchayaabhidhammavinayagāḷhasuttantaviggahapadanikkhepapadasandhi padavibhattinavaṅgajinasāsanavaraṃ suṇantenāpi na tappitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, mahāsamuddassa pañcamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena sutasomajātake –

“Furthermore, great king, the great ocean is not filled up by all the rivers that flow into it—the Ganges, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—nor by the streams of water from the sky. So too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of meditation, should not be sated even when hearing the excellent nine-fold teaching of the Conqueror, which includes recitation, questioning, listening, retention, analysis, the Abhidhamma and Vinaya, profound discourses, grammatical analysis, word placement, conjunction, and inflection. This, great king, is the fifth quality of the ocean to be adopted. This was stated, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods, in the Sutasoma Jātaka:”

“‘Aggi yathā tiṇakaṭṭhaṃ dahanto, na tappati sāgaro vā nadīhi;

Evampi ce evampi ve (syā.), evaṃ hi me (ka.) jā. 1 asītinipāte paṇḍitā rājaseṭṭha, sutvā na tappanti subhāsitenā’”ti.

“‘As fire is not sated by burning grass and wood, nor the ocean by the rivers; so too, O best of kings, the wise are not sated by hearing what is well-spoken.’”

Samuddaṅgapañho dasamo.Samuddavaggo dutiyo.

The Tenth Question on the Ocean's Qualities. The Second Chapter, on the Ocean, is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ [V 0.0349] –

The summary:

Lābulatā ca padumaṃ, bījaṃ sālakalyāṇikā;

Nāvā ca nāvālagganaṃ, kūpo niyāmako tathā;

Kammakāro samuddo ca, vaggo tena pavuccatīti.

The gourd creeper and the lotus, the seed and the beautiful Sāl tree; the ship, the anchor, the mast-socket, and the helmsman likewise; the workman and the ocean—by these the chapter is declared.

3. Pathavīvaggo

3. The Chapter on the Earth

1. Pathavīaṅgapañho

1. The Question on the Qualities of the Earth

1. “Bhante [V 0.0350][P 0.0382][M 0.0365] nāgasena, ‘pathaviyā pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, pathavī iṭṭhāniṭṭhāni kappūrāgarutagaracandanakuṅkumādīni ākirantepi pittasemhapubbaruhirasedamedakheḷasiṅghāṇikalasika- muttakarīsādīni ākirantepi tādisā yeva, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena iṭṭhāniṭṭhe lābhālābhe yasāyase nindāpasaṃsāya sukhadukkhe sabbattha tādinā yeva bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, pathaviyā paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

“Venerable Nāgasena, you say, ‘five qualities of the earth should be adopted.’ What are those five qualities that should be adopted?” “Just as, great king, the earth remains the same whether people scatter upon it desirable and undesirable things like camphor, agalloch, tagara, sandalwood, saffron, and so on, or scatter upon it bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, saliva, mucus, bilious liquid, urine, and feces—in the same way, great king, a yogi, devoted to practice, should be imperturbable in all circumstances, whether desirable or undesirable, gain or loss, fame or infamy, praise or blame, happiness or suffering. This, great king, is the first quality of the earth that should be adopted.”

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, pathavī maṇḍanavibhūsanāpagatā sakagandhaparibhāvitā, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena vibhūsanāpagatena sakasīlagandhaparibhāvitena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, pathaviyā dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

“Furthermore, great king, just as the earth is free from adornments and decorations, yet pervaded by its own fragrance, so too, great king, should a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, be free from adornments and decorations, yet pervaded by the fragrance of his own virtue. This, great king, is the second quality of the earth to be adopted.”

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, pathavī nirantarā akhaṇḍacchiddā asusirā bahalā ghanā vitthiṇṇā, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena nirantaramakhaṇḍacchiddamasusirabahalaghanavitthiṇṇasīlena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, pathaviyā tatiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, the earth is continuous, without breaks or holes, not hollow, thick, dense, and extensive. In the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should have morality that is continuous, without breaks or holes, not hollow, thick, dense, and extensive. This, great king, is the third quality of the earth to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, pathavī gāmanigamanagarajanapadarukkhapabbatanadītaḷākapokkharaṇīmigapakkhimanujanaranārigaṇaṃ dhārentīpi akilāsu hoti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena ovadantenapi anusāsantenapi viññāpentenapi sandassentenapi samādapentenapi samuttejentenapi sampahaṃsentenapi dhammadesanāsu akilāsunā bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, pathaviyā catutthaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, the earth, though bearing villages, towns, cities, districts, trees, mountains, rivers, lakes, ponds, herds of animals, flocks of birds, humans, men, and women, does not grow weary. In the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should not grow weary in giving discourses on the Dhamma—advising, instructing, informing, showing, establishing, arousing, and gladdening. This, great king, is the fourth quality of the earth to be adopted.

“Puna [V 0.0351] caparaṃ, mahārāja, pathavī anunayappaṭighavippamuttā, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena anunayappaṭighavippamuttena pathavisamena cetasā viharitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, pathaviyā pañcamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ[P 0.0383], mahārāja, upāsikāya cūḷasubhaddāya sakasamaṇe parikittayamānāya –

Furthermore, great king, the earth is free from attraction and repulsion; in the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should dwell with a mind like the earth, free from attraction and repulsion. This, great king, is the fifth quality of the earth to be adopted. This was also spoken, great king, by the female lay follower Cūḷasubhaddā while extolling her own ascetics:

“‘Ekañce [M 0.0366] bāhaṃ vāsiyā, tacche kupitamānasā kupitamānaso (ka.);

Ekañcebāhaṃ gandhena, ālimpeyya pamoditā pamodito (ka.).

‘If with an angry mind one should shave one arm with an adze, and if, delighted, one should anoint the other arm with perfume,

“‘Amusmiṃ paṭigho natthi, rāgo asmiṃ na vijjati;

Pathavīsamacittā te, tādisā samaṇā mamā’”ti.

‘Towards the former, there is no aversion; towards the latter, no lust is found. They have minds like the earth; such are my ascetics.’

Pathavīaṅgapañho paṭhamo.

The First Question on the Qualities of the Earth.

2. Āpaṅgapañho

2. The Question on the Qualities of Water

2. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘āpassa pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, āpo susaṇṭhitamakampitamaluḷitasabhāvaparisuddho, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena kuhanalapananemittakanippesikataṃ apanetvā susaṇṭhitamakampitamaluḷitasabhāvaparisuddhācārena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, āpassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

2. “Venerable Nāgasena, you say, ‘Five qualities of water are to be adopted.’ What are those five qualities to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, water is well-settled, unmoving, undisturbed, and naturally pure, so too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should abandon deceitfulness, talkativeness, hinting, and disparagement, and be endowed with conduct that is well-settled, unmoving, undisturbed, and naturally pure. This, great king, is the first quality of water to be adopted.”

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, āpo sītalasabhāvasaṇṭhito, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena sabbasattesu khantimettānuddayasampannena hitesinā anukampakena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, āpassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, water is established in a cool nature; in the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should be one who wishes for the welfare of all beings, who is compassionate and endowed with patience, loving-kindness, and sympathy. This, great king, is the second quality of water to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, āpo asuciṃ suciṃ karoti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena gāme vā araññe vā upajjhāye upajjhāyamattesu ācariye ācariyamattesu sabbattha anadhikaraṇena bhavitabbaṃ anavasesakārinā. Idaṃ, mahārāja, āpassa tatiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, water makes the impure pure; in the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, whether in the village or the forest, should be without disputes everywhere—towards preceptors, those like preceptors, teachers, or those like teachers—accomplishing everything without remainder. This, great king, is the third quality of water to be adopted.

“Puna [V 0.0352] caparaṃ, mahārāja, āpo bahujanapatthito, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena appicchasantuṭṭhapavivittapaṭisallānena satataṃ sabbalokamabhipatthitena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, āpassa catutthaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, water is desired by many people; in the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, being of few wishes, content, secluded, and devoted to solitude, should be constantly desired by the whole world. This, great king, is the fourth quality of water to be adopted.

“Puna [M 0.0367] caparaṃ, mahārāja, āpo na kassaci ahitamupadahati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena parabhaṇḍanakalahaviggahavivādarittajjhānaaratijananaṃ kāyavacīcittehi [P 0.0384] pāpakaṃ na karaṇīyaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, āpassa pañcamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ mahārāja, bhagavatā, devātidevena kaṇhajātake –

Furthermore, great king, water brings no harm to anyone; in the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should not do evil with body, speech, or mind, such as generating quarrels with others, disputes, conflicts, arguments, vain contemplation, or discontent. This, great king, is the fifth quality of water to be adopted. This was also spoken, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods, in the Kaṇha Jātaka:

“‘Varañce me ado sakka, sabbabhūtānamissara;

Na mano vā sarīraṃ vā, maṃ-kate sakka kassaci;

Kadāci upahaññetha, etaṃ sakka varaṃ vare’”ti.

‘If you, Sakka, lord of all beings, would grant me a boon, may neither the mind nor body of anyone whosoever ever be harmed on my account. This, O Sakka, is the boon I would choose.’

Āpaṅgapañho dutiyo.

The Second Question on the Qualities of Water.

3. Tejaṅgapañho

3. The Question on the Qualities of Fire

3. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘tejassa pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, tejo tiṇakaṭṭhasākhāpalāsaṃ ḍahati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena ye te abbhantarā vā bāhirā vā kilesā iṭṭhāniṭṭhārammaṇānubhavanā, sabbe te ñāṇagginā ḍahitabbā. Idaṃ, mahārāja, tejassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

3. “Venerable Nāgasena, you say, ‘Five qualities of fire are to be adopted.’ What are these five qualities to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, fire burns grass, sticks, branches, and leaves, so too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should burn up with the fire of knowledge all those internal and external defilements that consist in the experiencing of agreeable and disagreeable objects. This, great king, is the first quality of fire to be adopted.”

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, tejo niddayo akāruṇiko, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena sabbakilesesu kāruññānuddayā na kātabbā. Idaṃ, mahārāja, tejassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, fire is merciless and uncompassionate; in the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should not show compassion and sympathy toward any defilements. This, great king, is the second quality of fire to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, tejo sītaṃ paṭihanati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena [V 0.0353] vīriyasantāpatejaṃ abhijanetvā kilesā paṭihantabbā. Idaṃ, mahārāja, tejassa tatiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, fire overcomes cold; in the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, having generated the fiery heat of energy, should overcome the defilements. This, great king, is the third quality of fire to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, tejo anunayappaṭighavippamutto uṇhamabhijaneti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena anunayappaṭighavippamuttena tejosamena cetasā viharitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, tejassa catutthaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, fire, being free from attraction and repulsion, produces heat; in the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should dwell with a mind that is like fire, free from attraction and repulsion. This, great king, is the fourth quality of fire to be adopted.

“Puna [M 0.0368] caparaṃ, mahārāja, tejo andhakāraṃ vidhamitvā vidhamati (sī. pī. ka.) ālokaṃ dassayati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena avijjandhakāraṃ vidhamitvā ñāṇālokaṃ dassayitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, tejassa pañcamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena sakaṃ puttaṃ rāhulaṃ ovadantena [P 0.0385] –

Furthermore, great king, fire dispels darkness and reveals light; in the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should dispel the darkness of ignorance and reveal the light of knowledge. This, great king, is the fifth quality of fire to be adopted. This was also said, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods, when advising his own son Rāhula:

‘Tejosamaṃ ma. ni. 2.119, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi, tejosamaṃ hi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā? Manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassantī’”ti.

‘Rāhula, develop the meditation that is like fire. For when you, Rāhula, are developing the meditation that is like fire, arisen agreeable and disagreeable contacts will not take possession of your mind and remain.’

Tejaṅgapañho tatiyo.

The Third Question on the Qualities of Fire.

4. Vāyuṅgapañho

4. The Question on the Qualities of Wind

4. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘vāyussa pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, vāyu supupphitavanasaṇḍantaraṃ abhivāyati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena vimuttivarakusumapupphitārammaṇavanantare ramitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, vāyussa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

4. “Venerable Nāgasena, you say, ‘Five qualities of wind are to be adopted.’ What are these five qualities to be adopted?” “Just as, great king, the wind blows through a well-flowered forest grove, so too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should delight in the forest-like object of meditation that has blossomed with the excellent flowers of liberation. This, great king, is the first quality of wind to be adopted.”

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, vāyu dharaṇīruhapādapagaṇe mathayati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena vanantaragatena saṅkhāre vicinantena kilesā mathayitabbā. Idaṃ, mahārāja, vāyussa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, the wind churns up the host of trees growing on the earth; in the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, having gone into the forest and while investigating formations, should churn up the defilements. This, great king, is the second quality of wind to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, vāyu ākāse carati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena [V 0.0354] lokuttaradhammesu mānasaṃ sañcārayitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, vāyussa tatiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, the wind moves in space; in the same way, great king, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, should make his mind move among the supramundane states. This, great king, is the third quality of wind to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, vāyu gandhaṃ anubhavati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena attano sīlavarasurabhigandho sīlasurabhigando (sī. pī.) anubhavitabbo. Idaṃ, mahārāja, vāyussa catutthaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, just as the wind experiences a scent, so too, great king, should a yogi devoted to meditation experience the excellent, fragrant scent of his own virtue. This, great king, is the fourth quality of the wind to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, vāyu nirālayo aniketavāsī, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena nirālayamaniketamasanthavena sabbattha [M 0.0369] vimuttena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, vāyussa pañcamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena suttanipāte –

Furthermore, great king, just as the wind is without a home, not dwelling in a fixed abode, so too, great king, should a yogi devoted to meditation be without a home, without a fixed abode, without intimacy, and liberated in every respect. This, great king, is the fifth quality of the wind to be adopted. And this was spoken, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods, in the Suttanipāta:

“‘Santhavāto bhayaṃ jātaṃ, niketā jāyate rajo;

Aniketamasanthavaṃ, etaṃ ve munidassana’”nti.

'From intimacy, fear is born; from a home, dust arises. To be without a home and without intimacy—this truly is the vision of a sage.'

Vāyuṅgapañho catuttho.

The Fourth Question on the Qualities of the Wind is concluded.

5. Pabbataṅgapañho

5. The Question on the Qualities of a Mountain

5. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘pabbatassa pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti[P 0.0386]? “Yathā, mahārāja, pabbato acalo akampito akampiyo (sī. pī.) asampavedhī, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena sammānane vimānane sakkāre asakkāre garukāre agarukāre yase ayase nindāya pasaṃsāya sukhe dukkhe iṭṭhāniṭṭhesu sabbattha rūpasaddagandharasaphoṭṭhabbadhammesu rajanīyesu na rajjitabbaṃ, dussanīyesu na dussitabbaṃ, muyhanīyesu na muyhitabbaṃ, na kampitabbaṃ na calitabbaṃ, pabbatena viya acalena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, pabbatassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena –

5. "Venerable Nāgasena, you say, 'Five qualities of a mountain are to be adopted.' What are these five qualities to be adopted?" "Just as, great king, a mountain is unmoving, unshaken, and untrembling, so too, great king, should a yogi devoted to meditation—amidst honor and dishonor, respect and disrespect, reverence and irreverence, fame and infamy, blame and praise, pleasure and pain, and amidst all agreeable and disagreeable sights, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental objects—not be lustful toward what is enticing, not be hostile toward what is offensive, and not be deluded toward what is bewildering. He should not be shaken, he should not be moved; he should be unmoving like a mountain. This, great king, is the first quality of a mountain to be adopted. And this was spoken, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods:

“‘Selo [V 0.0355] yathā ekaghano ekagghano (ka.) dha. pa. 81 dhammapade, vātena na samīrati;

Evaṃ nindāpasaṃsāsu, na samiñjanti paṇḍitā’ti.

'As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, so the wise are not moved by blame and praise.'

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, pabbato thaddho na kenaci saṃsaṭṭho, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena thaddhena asaṃsaṭṭhena bhavitabbaṃ, na kenaci saṃsaggo karaṇīyo. Idaṃ, mahārāja, pabbatassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena –

Furthermore, great king, a mountain is firm and not associated with anything; so too, great king, should a yogi devoted to meditation be firm and unassociated, not forming an intimacy with anyone. This, great king, is the second quality of a mountain to be adopted. And this was spoken, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods:

“‘Asaṃsaṭṭhaṃ gahaṭṭhehi, anāgārehi cūbhayaṃ;

Anokasārimappicchaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇa’nti.

'Unassociated with both householders and the homeless, wandering without a home, of few wishes—that one I call a brahmin.'

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, pabbate bījaṃ na virūhati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena sakamānase kilesā na virūhāpetabbā. Idaṃ, mahārāja, pabbatassa tatiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, therena subhūtinā –

Furthermore, great king, just as a seed does not sprout on a mountain, so too, great king, should a yogi devoted to meditation not allow the defilements to sprout in his own mind. This, great king, is the third quality of a mountain to be adopted. And this was spoken, great king, by the Elder Subhūti:

“‘Rāgūpasaṃhitaṃ [M 0.0370] cittaṃ, yadā uppajjate mama;

Sayaṃva paccavekkhāmi paccavekkhitvā (sabbattha), ekaggo ekako (sabbattha) taṃ damemahaṃ.

'When a mind connected with lust arises in me, I myself reflect upon it; being concentrated, I subdue it.

“‘Rajjase rajjasi (sī.), rañjasi (pī.) rajanīye ca, dussanīye ca dussase;

Muyhase muyhasi (sī.) mohanīye ca, nikkhamassu vanā tuvaṃ.

'You are lustful toward the lust-inducing, you are hostile toward the hostility-inducing, and you are deluded by the delusion-inducing. You, get out of this forest!

“‘Visuddhānaṃ [P 0.0387] ayaṃ vāso, nimmalānaṃ tapassinaṃ;

Mā kho visuddhaṃ dūsesi, nikkhamassu vanā tuva’nti.

'This is the dwelling of the pure, of stainless ascetics. Do not defile this pure place! You, get out of this forest!'

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, pabbato accuggato, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena ñāṇaccuggatena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, pabbatassa catutthaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena –

Furthermore, great king, just as a mountain is exceedingly lofty, so too, great king, should a yogi devoted to meditation be exceedingly lofty in wisdom. This, great king, is the fourth quality of a mountain to be adopted. And this was spoken, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods:

“‘Pamādaṃ appamādena, yadā nudati paṇḍito;

Paññāpāsādamāruyha, asoko sokiniṃ pajaṃ;

Pabbataṭṭhova bhūmaṭṭhe bhummaṭṭhe (sī. pī.), dhīro bāle avekkhatī’ti.

'When the wise one drives out heedlessness with heedfulness, having ascended the palace of wisdom, sorrowless he observes the sorrowing people. As one standing on a mountain observes those on the ground, so the steadfast one observes the fools.'

“Puna [V 0.0356] caparaṃ, mahārāja, pabbato anunnato anonato, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena unnatāvanati na karaṇīyā. Idaṃ, mahārāja, pabbatassa pañcamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, upāsikāya cūḷasubhaddāya sakasamaṇe parikittayamānāya –

Furthermore, great king, a mountain is neither elevated nor depressed; so too, great king, a yogi devoted to meditation should not practice elation or dejection. This, great king, is the fifth quality of a mountain to be adopted. And this was spoken, great king, by the female lay follower Cūḷasubhaddā while extolling her own ascetics:

“‘Lābhena unnato loko, alābhena ca onato;

Lābhālābhena ekatthā ekaṭṭhā (sī. pī.), tādisā samaṇā mamā’”ti.

'The world is elated by gain and dejected by loss; but in gain and loss, they remain the same—such are my ascetics.'

Pabbataṅgapañho pañcamo.

The Fifth Question on the Qualities of a Mountain is concluded.

6. Ākāsaṅgapañho

6. The Question on the Qualities of Space

6. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘ākāsassa pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, ākāso sabbaso agayho, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena [M 0.0371] sabbaso kilesehi agayhena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, ākāsassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

6. "Venerable Nāgasena, you say, 'Five qualities of space are to be adopted.' What are these five qualities to be adopted?" "Just as, great king, space is entirely ungraspable, so too, great king, should a yogi devoted to meditation be entirely ungraspable by the defilements. This, great king, is the first quality of space to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, ākāso isitāpasabhūtadijagaṇānusañcarito, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena ‘aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattā’ti saṅkhāresu mānasaṃ sañcārayitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, ākāsassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, just as space is traversed by multitudes of seers, ascetics, beings, and birds, so too, great king, should a yogi devoted to meditation cause his mind to roam among conditioned phenomena with the thought, ‘Impermanent, suffering, non-self.’ This, great king, is the second quality of space to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, ākāso santāsanīyo, evameva kho, mahārāja[P 0.0388], yoginā yogāvacarena sabbabhavapaṭisandhīsu mānasaṃ ubbejayitabbaṃ, assādo na kātabbo. Idaṃ, mahārāja, ākāsassa tatiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, just as space is terrifying, so too, great king, should a yogi devoted to meditation make his mind recoil from rebirth in any state of existence, and he should not take delight therein. This, great king, is the third quality of space to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, ākāso ananto appamāṇo aparimeyyo, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena anantasīlena aparimitañāṇena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, ākāsassa catutthaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, just as space is endless, boundless, and immeasurable, so too, great king, should a yogi devoted to meditation be of endless virtue and immeasurable wisdom. This, great king, is the fourth quality of space to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, ākāso alaggo asatto appatiṭṭhito apalibuddho, evameva kho[V 0.0357], mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena kule gaṇe lābhe āvāse palibodhe paccaye sabbakilesesu ca sabbattha alaggena bhavitabbaṃ, anāsattena appatiṭṭhitena apalibuddhena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, ākāsassa pañcamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena sakaṃ puttaṃ rāhulaṃ ovadantena – ‘seyyathāpi, rāhula ma. ni. 2.119, ākāso na katthaci patiṭṭhito, evameva kho tvaṃ, rāhula, ākāsasamaṃ bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi, ākāsasamaṃ hi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhassantī’”ti.

Furthermore, great king, just as space is unattached, unclinging, unestablished, and unobstructed, so too, great king, should a yogi devoted to meditation be unattached everywhere—to families, groups, gains, dwellings, impediments, requisites, and to all defilements; he should be unclinging, unestablished, and unobstructed. This, great king, is the fifth quality of space to be adopted. And this was spoken, great king, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods, while advising his own son Rāhula: ‘Just as, Rāhula, space is not established anywhere, so too, Rāhula, should you develop a meditation like space. For when you, Rāhula, develop a meditation like space, pleasant and unpleasant contacts that arise will not overcome your mind and remain.’

Ākāsaṅgapañho chaṭṭho.

The Sixth Question on the Qualities of Space is concluded.

7. Candaṅgapañho

7. The Question on the Qualities of the Moon

7. “Bhante nāgasena, ‘candassa pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī’ti yaṃ vadesi, katamāni tāni pañca aṅgāni gahetabbānī”ti? “Yathā, mahārāja, cando sukkapakkhe [M 0.0372] udayanto uttaruttariṃ vaḍḍhati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena ācārasīlaguṇavattappaṭipattiyā āgamādhigame paṭisallāne satipaṭṭhāne indriyesu guttadvāratāya bhojane mattaññutāya jāgariyānuyoge uttaruttariṃ vaḍḍhitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, candassa paṭhamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

7. "Venerable Nāgasena, you say, 'Five qualities of the moon are to be adopted.' What are these five qualities to be adopted?" "Just as, great king, the moon, having arisen in the bright fortnight, waxes ever more and more, so too, great king, should a yogi devoted to meditation grow ever more and more in the practice of virtuous conduct, moral qualities, and observances; in scriptural learning and spiritual attainment; in seclusion; in the establishments of mindfulness; in guarding the sense-doors; in moderation in eating; and in the practice of wakefulness. This, great king, is the first quality of the moon to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, cando uḷārādhipati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena uḷārena chandādhipatinā bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, candassa dutiyaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, the moon is an eminent overlord. Just so, great king, a yogi, a practitioner, should be one with noble aspiration as his master. This, great king, is the second quality of the moon to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, cando nisāya carati, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena pavivittena bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, candassa tatiyaṃ [P 0.0389] aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, the moon travels by night. Just so, great king, a yogi, a practitioner, should be one who dwells in solitude. This, great king, is the third quality of the moon to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, cando vimānaketu, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā yogāvacarena sīlaketunā bhavitabbaṃ. Idaṃ, mahārāja, candassa catutthaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, great king, the moon is a banner of the celestial mansion. Just so, great king, a yogi, a practitioner, should be one whose banner is virtue. This, great king, is the fourth quality of the moon to be adopted.

“Puna caparaṃ, mahārāja, cando āyācitapatthito udeti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yoginā [V 0.0358] yogāvacarena āyācitapatthitena kulāni upasaṅkamitabbāni. Idaṃ, mahārāja, candassa pañcamaṃ aṅgaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Bhāsitampetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā devātidevena saṃyuttanikāyavare ‘candūpamā, bhikkhave, kulāni upasaṅkamatha, apakasseva kāyaṃ apakassa cittaṃ niccanavakā kulesu appagabbhā’”ti appagabbāti (ka.) saṃ. ni. 2.146.

Furthermore, great king, the moon rises requested and longed for. So too, great king, a yogi, a practitioner, should approach families, being requested and longed for. This, great king, is the fifth quality of the moon to be adopted.
